properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 10 at 4:53PM PDT until September 10 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat risk this afternoon will be moderate to major.

* WHERE...A portion of central California.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Major risk of heat-related illnesses for much
of the population, especially those without effective cooling or
hydration.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 10 at 3:42PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

UPDATE: Based on forecast winds and water levels, flooding continues
to look very unlikely along Kuskokwim River and the coast. However,
higher water levels and winds gusting up to 30 to 45 mph may still
impact activities along the water.

For communities along Kuskokwim River (Tuntutuliak):
* Gusty winds and storm surge pushing up the river will likely cause
water levels to reach bankfull.
* Flooding will be very unlikely as high water currently in McGrath
and Crooked Creek is now forecast to arrive in the lower Kuskokwim
River after the storm surge has subsided.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide, which will
be from around 11 AM through 3 PM on Friday.

For communities along the coast (Kongiganak, Kwigillingok, Kipnuk,
Toksook Bay, Tununak):
* Though there will be gusty onshore winds and storm surge, water
levels will very likely remain below 1 to 2 feet above the normal
highest tide, with no flooding expected.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide on Friday,
from about 10 AM through 2 PM. Communities further north (like
Toksook Bay and Tununak) may see higher water levels during
Thursday nights high tide as well, from about 10 PM through 2 AM.

Next steps:
* Use caution along Kuskokwim River and along the coast, and plan for
higher than normal water levels.
* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 25.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 PM CDT Thursday was 25.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
evening and continue falling to 18.9 feet early Tuesday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 25.0
feet on 10/29/1975.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 10 at 1:52PM CDT until September 10 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING FOR
LOCATIONS IN NORTH DAKOTA SOUTH AND WEST OF THE MISSOURI RIVER AND
LAKE SAKAKAWEA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over much of western and
parts of south central North Dakota today ahead of an approaching
cold front. Temperatures are forecast to climb into the upper 80s,
with afternoon humidity values as low as 13 percent. Winds this
afternoon are forecast to be southwest to west around 15 mph with
gusts to 30 mph. Due to the low humidity and breezy conditions with
abundant dry vegetation, critical fire weather conditions are
expected to continue into early this evening for locations in North
Dakota to the south and west of the Missouri River and Lake
Sakakawea.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of North Dakota south and west of the
Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea.

* TIMING...Until 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...Southwest to west around 15 mph with gusts to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity as low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.
